questions.question:
Directions: Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space with four options. Select whichever preposition or determiner you consider the most appropriate for the blank space and indicate your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

His funeral will be private, in accordance _______ his wishes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘with’.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The above sentence is an example of a preposition.
 
• A preposition is a word used to link nouns, pronouns, or phrases to other words within a sentence.
 
• As per the general rule, '**in accordance with**' is a prepositional phrase which means "**if something is done in accordance with a particular rule or system, it is done in the way that the rule or system says that it should be done**".
 
• Example:​
 
 
• *The soldiers said they acted **in accordance with** his orders. (correct)*
 
• *The soldiers said they acted **in accordance to/at** his orders. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• *​*According to the explanation and example that are given above, ‘with’ is the correct choice for the given blank.

Correct sentence: *His funeral will be private, **in accordance with** his wishes.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.**

Most of the members at the meeting felt (a)/ that the group appointed for investigating the case (b)/ were not competent to do the job efficiently. (c)/ No error.(d)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'c'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The error lies in the usage of 'were' instead of 'was'.
 
• As the **helping verb **'*were*' in the **c part **of the sentence is used for the **subject **'*the group*' which shows the collectiveness of people here, the usage of 'were' is inappropriate.
 
• When we express the **subject **as a **collection of something or someone**, then it is followed by the **singular form of the verb** whether it is a **helping verb(is/was/has)** or **main verb(V5)**.
 
 
• ​For example:- The group **has **been notoriously fickle in the past.
 
 
 
• Thus, '*were*' in the **c part** of the sentence should be **replaced **with '*was*' in order to make the given sentence **grammatically correct**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2. 

Correct Sentence: *Most of the members at the meeting felt that the group appointed for investigating the case **was **not competent to do the job efficiently. *

questions.question:
**Choose the correct form of adjective for the given sentence:**

My father has ______ patience than my mother who loses her temper for trivial things.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'more'.

***__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ​As in the given sentence, we are talking about **the speaker's father, who has more patience than his/her mother, who loses her temper for trivial things.***
 
• Here, the comparative degree of an adjective is used as we are comparing *the patience level of the speaker's father with his/her mother's level.*
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Adjectives have three degrees that compare one thing to another.
 
• The three degrees of adjectives are *positive, comparative, and superlative.*
 
 
• The Positive degree is the uncompared base form of an adjective or adverb.
 
• It offers no comparison.
 
• ​For example:- ​*Jack is **as tall as** Ram.*
 
• A comparative adjective is an adjective used to compare two people or things.
 
• We use comparative adjectives to say that one person or thing demonstrates a high degree of quality or is a better example of a quality than the other.
 
• ​For example:- *Jack is **taller **than his cousin.*
 
• Superlative adjectives are used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of quality.
 
• They are used in sentences where a subject is compared to a group of objects.
 
• ​For example:- *My house is the **largest **one in our neighborhood.*
